sections.h2: How is Billings laid out, and why does it matter for a house sale?
sections.html:
Billings sits in the Yellowstone Valley at 3,126 feet and is split by the Rims, a line of sandstone cliffs also called the Rimrocks. According to Wikipedia's summary of Census data, the city covers about 43.5 square miles of land, with two-thirds in the Yellowstone Valley and the South Hills and one-third in the Heights and Lockwood area.

The cliffs run north and east of downtown. The northern face is about 500 feet tall and the eastern face about 800 feet, which separates downtown from the Heights to the north and Lockwood to the east. Billings Logan International Airport sits on top of the Rims.

  • Downtown and the valley floor: older housing near the Yellowstone River.
  • Billings Heights: north of the Rims, along U.S. Highway 87, called Main Street inside the city.
  • Lockwood: east of downtown, linked to the Heights by the planned Billings Bypass.
  • South Hills, West End and Shiloh: reached by Interstate 90 and Montana Highway 3.

The cliffs also make the Rimrocks a landmark. Billings has more than 50 miles of trails in and around the city, including about seven continuous miles along the top of the Rims, and seven mountain ranges are visible from town. A house with a view of the Rims or an easy route onto the trail system has features a listing can point to.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Billings, Montana?
sections.html:
Billings was founded in 1877 and incorporated on March 24, 1882. It is named for Frederick H. Billings, a former president of the Northern Pacific Railroad. The area was earlier known as Clark's Fork Bottom.

The first town in the Yellowstone Valley was Coulson, formed in 1877 around a sawmill and a trading post. When the Northern Pacific came through, the railroad owned two adjoining sections about two miles west of Coulson and chose to build a new town there. Most Coulson residents gradually moved to the new town, and Boothill Cemetery is the only physical trace left of Coulson.

The Crow have lived in the Billings area since about 1700, and the present-day Crow Nation lies just south of the city. William Clark passed through in July 1806 and carved his name on Pompey's Pillar east of town.

sections.h2: What does the Billings economy look like?
sections.html:
Healthcare is the largest employment sector. Billings Clinic employs about 4,500 people and St. Vincent Regional Hospital about 2,200, and together they anchor a growing medical corridor.

HealthcareBillings Clinic about 4,500 employees; St. Vincent Regional Hospital about 2,200
EnergyThe three largest of Montana's four oil refineries are in Yellowstone County
AgricultureWestern Sugar Cooperative plant processes sugar beets; two of the state's 13 livestock auctions
HeadquartersKampgrounds of America and First Interstate Bank
ManufacturingCoca-Cola, Franz Bakery and Meadow Gold facilities
RetailMontana has no sales tax; about $1 of every $7 in state retail spending happens in Billings

The Billings trade area serves over half a million people.

sections.h2: How does Billings weather affect an older house?
sections.html:
Billings has a cold semi-arid climate with hot, dry summers and cold, dry winters. Snowfall averages 57.4 inches a year, but warm chinook winds mean snow does not usually stay long. The snowiest year on record was 2017 to 2018, at 106.1 inches.

  • Temperatures reach 100 degrees on an average of 1 to 3 days a year and fall below 0 on about 12.9 days.
  • The first freeze of the season arrives by about October 6 and the last by about May 5.
  • On June 20, 2010, a tornado touched down in the Heights and downtown with hail up to golf ball size, and it severely damaged the MetraPark Arena.

Hail is the item for roof inspections. A buyer's inspector may flag aging shingles, and a seller who wants to skip a repair negotiation can sell the house as is.

sections.h2: What schools and roads serve Billings?
sections.html:
Billings Public Schools includes the Billings Elementary and Billings High School districts, with 21 elementary schools, six middle schools and three high schools: Senior High, Skyview High and West High. Other elementary districts that cover parts of Billings are Blue Creek, Elder Grove, Canyon Creek, Elysian and Independent.

Interstate 90 runs east to west through the south of the city, and Interstate 94 meets it east of downtown. U.S. 87 through the Heights is described as the busiest section of roadway in Montana. The Billings Bypass is planned to link the Heights and Lockwood, and its new Yellowstone River bridge was completed in 2023.

Montana State University Billings, founded in 1927 as a normal school and known as Eastern Montana College from 1949 to 1994, enrolls around 4,100 students. Private options include Billings Catholic Schools, with about 1,000 students, and Billings Christian School.

Billings METropolitan Transit runs fixed-route and paratransit buses, with downtown and West End transit centers. Amtrak's North Coast Hiawatha last stopped at the Billings Depot in 1979.

sections.h2: How is property tax handled in Billings and Yellowstone County?
sections.html:
Billings homes are taxed through the Yellowstone County Treasurer, currently Hank Peters, at 2825 3rd Avenue North, Room 113, phone 406-256-2802. The county says the department collects about $345 million a year and processes roughly 75,000 real estate, 5,900 mobile home and 1,050 personal property tax bills.

ItemYellowstone County rule
Real estate, first halfNovember 30 (2026 only: December 3)
Real estate, second halfMay 31 (2027 only: June 1)
Deadline time5 p.m. Mountain Time, next business day if a weekend or holiday
Late payment2% penalty and 5/6 of 1% interest per month

The Department of Revenue's 2026 rates give primary residences and long-term rentals a tiered scale beginning at 0.76% on the first $378,000, while second homes, short-term rentals and vacant lots pay 1.90%. An owner who disagrees with a valuation has 30 days from the notice date to file Form AB-26, or may appeal directly to the county tax appeal board.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a house in Billings?
sections.html:
There are three routes: list with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer. Each carries different costs, timelines and risks under Montana law.

  • List with an agent: exposure to more buyers, plus commission, showings and repairs a buyer's inspection may request.
  • Sell it yourself: you save commission and handle the marketing, contract and paperwork.
  • Cash offer: a direct purchase, usually as is, with a closing date you choose.

Whichever route you take, the deed has to be acknowledged and recorded with the county clerk and recorder, a Realty Transfer Certificate has to accompany it, and the standard recording fee is $20 for the first page and $10 for each added page. Any unpaid property tax is a lien on the house and gets paid at closing.

If you want a cash offer on a Billings house, tell us about the property in the form above. We reply with a written offer, and you owe nothing if you turn it down.

sections.h2: What paperwork closes a house sale in Billings?
sections.html:
The closing file for a Billings house includes a deed, a Realty Transfer Certificate and the recording fee, all filed with the county clerk and recorder. The Department of Revenue says the certificate collects sale price information used in the mass appraisal of Montana real property, so the price you report can show up later in how nearby homes are valued.

  • Seller and buyer names must match on the certificate and the deed.
  • The certificate asks for the last four digits of each party's Social Security or employer identification number.
  • The deed must be acknowledged before a notary before it can be recorded.

Once recorded, the deed is constructive notice to later buyers and lenders from the time of filing.

faqs.a: The 2025 Census Bureau estimate is 121,239 residents. The city covers about 43.5 square miles of land and sits at 3,126 feet in the Yellowstone Valley.

faqs.q: When are Yellowstone County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half of real estate tax is due November 30, with December 3 as the 2026 date, and the second half is due May 31, with June 1 in 2027. Payments are due by 5 p.m. Mountain Time.

faqs.q: Who is the largest employer in Billings?
faqs.a: Healthcare is the largest sector. Billings Clinic employs about 4,500 people and St. Vincent Regional Hospital about 2,200.
Yes. A June 20, 2010 tornado came with hail up to golf ball size and damaged downtown, the Heights and the MetraPark Arena. Roof condition is a common point in a Billings sale.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Billings house as is?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can purchase a Billings house in its present condition, and the sale still requires a recorded deed and a Realty Transfer Certificate.
